prompt_text: What is the best AI video ad maker?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “best” AI video ad maker — the right tool depends on your goals (platform, style, budget, and whether you need talking‑head presenters, animated templates, or automated repurposing). Below are the top options (as of my last update) and when to pick each one — plus a quick checklist so I can recommend one for your exact needs.

Top picks and when to use them
- Canva Video
  - Best for: fastest, easiest social ads (Instagram/Facebook/TikTok) using templates.
  - Pros: huge template library, brand kit, text-to-video features, tons of export presets.
  - Cons: less advanced generative video realism than specialized AI tools.

- Synthesia / HeyGen / Elai.io
  - Best for: AI presenters/talking‑head ads (brand spokesperson without filming).
  - Pros: realistic avatars, many languages and voice options, quick script → video.
  - Cons: limited scene types (mostly talking heads), cost scales with usage.

- Pictory / Lumen5 / Vidyo.ai
  - Best for: repurposing long-form content (blogs, webinars) into short ads.
  - Pros: auto-summarize, captioning, fast turnaround.
  - Cons: templates can feel generic unless customized.

- Promo.com / Biteable / InVideo (Vimeo Create)
  - Best for: ad-focused stock clips + templates for conversion-oriented creatives.
  - Pros: big licensed stock libraries, ad templates optimized for performance.
  - Cons: customization limits vs full editors.

- Kapwing / Descript
  - Best for: collaborative editing and rapid short-form edits (cuts, captions, voice-over).
  - Pros: easy trimming, caption auto-generation, good for social formats.
  - Cons: less template-based automation.

- Runway (text-to-video + advanced generative tools)
  - Best for: creative, non‑stock visuals and experimental ads that need novel imagery.
  - Pros: powerful generative models and compositing.
  - Cons: learning curve; outputs may need refinement.

- AdCreative.ai (paired with a video tool)
  - Best for: generating lots of ad variants and copy for testing.
  - Pros: speeds up creative ideation and A/B variant production.
  - Cons: typically focused on images/copy; pair with another video generator.

How to choose quickly
1. Platform & format: short vertical (TikTok/Reels) vs horizontal (YouTube).
2. Style: talking‑head, animated text, stock-footage montage, or novel generative visuals.
3. Volume: single hero ad vs dozens of variants for A/B testing.
4. Budget: free/trial tools vs enterprise subscriptions and per‑minute charges.
5. Need for localization: multiple languages/voices or dynamic personalization?

If you tell me:
- Which platform(s) you’re targeting,
- The ad style you want (talking head, animated, montage, repurposed clip),
- Approx. budget (free, <$50/month, $50–500/month, enterprise),
I’ll recommend 2–3 specific tools and a suggested workflow (script → assets → quick edits → export) and can even draft a sample 15s ad script for you. Note: my product info is current through mid‑2024; if you want the latest pricing or new entrants from 2024–2026 I can fetch that if you allow me to search the web.
